claims.claim: The arbitrary-sharing-number no-teleport problem belongs to NP.
claims.evidence: Let L be the number of feature occurrences. Every no-teleport transition has a feature live at both endpoint tiles and deletes at least those two occurrences, so a play has at most floor(L/2) transitions. A certificate is therefore a polynomial-length tile sequence. A verifier tracks live occurrences, checks distinct consecutive tiles and a nonempty live intersection, deletes every common live feature at both endpoints, and finally checks that no occurrence remains. This is polynomial time. The draft's additional pair-nonrepetition observation is also correct: the first use deletes every then-live common feature, and deleted occurrences never become live again.
claims.search_method: Direct invariant and certificate-verifier proof; the exact checker also asserts that every generated legal transition removes at least two occurrences.

claims.claim: There is an exact characterization by perfect matchings plus an ordered Euler trail with precedence constraints.
claims.evidence: Necessity: for each feature f, the moves that delete its occurrences pair all vertices of S_f, producing a perfect matching M_f. Every move deletes some feature, so every move edge belongs to the simple union H; no unordered pair can recur, making the play an Euler trail of H. If a nonmatching H-edge joins two f-vertices, at least one endpoint occurrence must already have been deleted by its matching edge, yielding the stated precedence disjunction. Sufficiency follows by an earliest-failure argument. If the earliest matching edge m_f(u) failed because u had been deleted on an earlier nonmatching edge uw, the constraint, since m_f(u) is later, forces m_f(w) before uw. By minimality that earlier matching edge successfully deleted w, so uw could not have deleted u—a contradiction. Hence all matching edges delete their intended live pairs. Every H-edge belongs to some matching and is therefore a legal transition, and all occurrences are deleted. Exact enumeration independently agreed with the characterization on all 139 families of distinct even support types through four tiles.
claims.search_method: Completed both directions using a minimal-counterexample argument, then exhaustively compared the characterization with direct play search on all even-support families through four labeled tiles.

claims.claim: If every occurring feature appears on exactly two tiles, no-teleport solvability is decidable in linear time even with unbounded sharing number.
claims.evidence: For a feature supported exactly on {u,v}, only transition uv can delete it, and both occurrences remain live until that transition. After collapsing all equal endpoint pairs, a solution is therefore exactly an Euler trail using every edge of the resulting simple graph K. Thus the criterion is connectivity of the edge-bearing vertices and zero or two odd degrees; the featureless instance is trivially solved. On the standard word-RAM/array-indexed representation, scan occurrences to obtain endpoint pairs, compress nonempty tile identifiers, radix-sort the two integer endpoints in linear time, deduplicate, and perform connectivity and parity tests, all in O(L) time. Arbitrarily many features may share one endpoint pair without affecting the argument. Exact enumeration confirmed the equivalence for all 1,099 simple graphs through five vertices and also tested duplicated endpoint pairs.
claims.search_method: Reduction to the Euler-trail criterion with a deterministic radix-sorting implementation analysis, supplemented by exhaustive exact graph enumeration.

claims.claim: The obvious static relaxation—choosing feature-perfect-matchings whose simple union is Eulerian—is not sufficient.
claims.evidence: The five-tile instance is a valid counterexample. The three two-tile features force triangle edges 01, 02, and 12. Because tiles 3 and 4 contain only their respective four-support feature, they must be the two endpoints of any no-teleport play. If their incident edges attach to core vertices i and j, Euler parity forces i=j. Starting at 3, the play takes 3i, must traverse the core triangle as a circuit based at i, and ends with i4. The first triangle edge from i encounters the feature supported on {0,1,2,4} live at both core endpoints and deletes its occurrence at i, so the final move to tile 4 cannot be legal; reversing the play gives the symmetric contradiction. Nevertheless, matchings 03+12 and 04+12 for the four-support features, together with forced matchings 01, 02, and 12, have simple union {01,02,12,03,04}, which is connected with exactly odd vertices 3 and 4. The exact checker explored 95 dynamic states, found no solution, found four Euler-trail orders for the displayed union, and found none satisfying precedence.
claims.witness: Tiles 0,1,2,3,4 with feature supports {0,1}, {0,2}, {1,2}, {0,1,2,3}, and {0,1,2,4}; static matchings are 01, 02, 12, (03+12), and (04+12).
claims.search_method: Analytic endpoint/parity contradiction plus exhaustive exact bit-set search over every legal start and transition, every perfect-matching choice, and every Euler-trail order for the witness.

claims.claim: An exact state-space algorithm runs in O(n^2 L·2^L) time and O(n·2^L) space.
claims.evidence: A state is (current tile, live-occurrence mask), giving at most n·2^L states. For each state, inspect all n−1 possible next tiles. Scanning the incidence representation identifies every feature live at both endpoints and constructs the successor mask in O(L) time. A transition exists exactly when this set is nonempty, and it strictly decreases the live-occurrence count, so memoized reachability is exact and acyclic. Trying every initial tile shares the same memo table. The resulting bound is O(n^2 L·2^L) time. A directly indexed Boolean table has n·2^L entries, giving O(n·2^L) words/bits up to the usual RAM convention, with lower-order instance and recursion storage.
claims.search_method: State-count, transition-cost, and acyclicity proof; implemented the recurrence with exact integer bit sets and cross-checked it against the matching characterization on bounded exhaustive instances.

target_evidence: The exact target requires a complete complexity classification for arbitrary sharing number, specifically either a polynomial-time algorithm or a matching hardness result. The draft establishes NP membership, an exact reformulation, an unrestricted-sharing special case, a failed-relaxation witness, and an exponential algorithm, but supplies neither required general result. These are material and correct advances, so the target verdict is VALID_PARTIAL_PROGRESS rather than FULLY_RESOLVES_TARGET. Separately, claimed_resolution is PARTIAL and the final writeup expressly says the full classification remains unresolved; that description is ACCURATE and neither overstated nor understated.
